steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook squash and onion in hot oil, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, mix together eggs, 1 cup Cheddar cheese, milk, sugar, flour, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Stir in squash mixture and melted butter; transfer to a 2-quart casserole dish. Top with remaining 2 cups Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until casserole is set and cheese is crisp and starting to brown, 35 to 45 minutes. Allow to stand for 15 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash, Egg, and Cheese Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Summer squash is baked with lots of Cheddar cheese and eggs for a casserole that will make everyone want to take seconds.
raw_recipe.name: Squash, Egg, and Cheese Casserole

review.reviewBody: I followed a reviewer's suggestion and added some orange bell pepper. It tasted great, but I didn't like the giant glob of cheese on top. Next time, I will mix in more cheese with the eggs and sprinkle a thin layer of cheese on top along with some bread crumbs.

I wanted this to be more of a breakfast casserole, so I diced the squash, and added 1 lb ground sausage, 2 additional eggs (6 total), 2 Tbsp more milk (4 Tbsp total), and 1 tsp. ground mustard. I decreased the butter to 4 Tbsp. I browned the sausage before adding if to the squash/butter/egg mixture. I also mixed in 2 c. of cheese. I put the last 1 c. of cheese across the top. I omitted the sugar and flour as well.

To be fair, I made a lot of changes, but I think some of them were definitely for the better. I took advice from other reviewers.
I didn't have summer squash on hand, so I used one of each: butternut, kabocha, and acorn. I precooked them in the microwave and they worked very well. If I were to use summer squash next time I would definitely use more than 3.
I used coconut oil instead of vegetable oil.
Added 4 cloves of minced garlic
6 eggs instead of 4
4 Tbsp milk
2 cups shredded mozzarella mixed in and 1 cup shredded cheddar on top (any cheese that can be shredded would work)
No flour or sugar (it was plenty sweet - I wouldn't have been able to eat it with the sugar, and the eggs held the casserole together no problem)
S&P as described, though perhaps a little extra salt may have worked (cheese is so salty, so I was nervous about that)
No butter (why add extra fat? It definitely was not needed. Cheese provides all the fat this dish needs)
Diced bell pepper
1 tsp dijon mustard - I'm going to use 1 Tbsp next time.
I served it with hot sauce and veggies on the side.
I may add mushrooms next time.

This wasn't a big hit with my family, but it's nice and healthy and vegetarian, so I'm adding it to my rotation.

Very good. I did adjust a little. I used only 4 tablespoons of butter, and did not use the sugar. I added a little bell pepper. Lastly, I used 1 1/2 cups cheese in the casserole, and then put 1 1/2 cups on top in the last 15 minutes of baking, thus preventing a thick hard crust. Less butter and no sugar did not hurt this recipe at all.

I use two large zucchini and add diced garlic while sautéing the zucchini and onion. I cover the top with one cup of shredded cheese instead of two so it comes out with a thin layer of crispy cheese. My family loves it, especially when served with ham and roasted potatoes.
Added salt to veggies while they cooked, added chalula sauce, chives, breadcrumbs, put more cheese in the sauce and less on top, less sugar, used cornmeal instead of flour.

My husband and I thought this was delicious! I cut the butter down to 4 Tbsp, used 5 squash, and only used 2 cups shredded cheese. Mixed in most of the cheese, and just saved a little to top with. We did think it was very sweet. I will cut it down to 1 Tbsp of sugar next time. Serve with some green beans, and this is a perfect meatless dinner.

It makes a lot, its very filling and good for side dish for the next night or a quick lunch that won't weigh you down! When I reheat a slice, I melted American cheese to the top and it was yummy! Great addition, oh and I crushed up some bread crumbs for the top and put less cheddar on the top, most went inside the dish.

This is a wonderful base start. I didn’t have enough cheddar so I used some truffle goat cheese to. I added some spicy yaggers (sausage) and Canadian bacon. Threw in a little broccoli that needed to be used up. I omitted the sugar.

This is VERY similar to the casserole I came up w/ only I didn't write down the measurements so I'm glad to see this one for next time. I opted to use a little more squash (5 small ones) and add a buttery bread crumb topping. My kiddos and hubby really liked it!I think adding finely diced green pepper would be good too. I ate the leftovers for breakfast the next morning and it was wonderful! If you add ham, it could make a great brunch dish! Thanks for posting!!
I added sliced zucchini and chopped bell peppers to the recipe. I used only half the cheese and no butter or sugar. It was very easy to make, tasty and filling. I will make it again.

I heeded the warning of a few reviewers who said the extra cheese was not needed...I only put in one cup of cheddar. The sugar was probably not necessary either since my squash is so sweet. And probably did not need quite so much butter. I liked this and will make it again.
Really good used mozzarella less cheese but still good was unsure about the sugar but yes it's really good with carrots

I found this to be a very strange casserole. With only 3 eggs to 3 squash and 3 cups of cheese? The portions seemed way off to me. Plus, the flour and sugar gave it a strange consistency and flavor. I think I would change this drastically to suit my tastes (i.e. more eggs, less cheese, no butter, extra seasonings, and definitely no flour or sugar). Sorry, but I don't think I'll make it again. Thanks for sharing your recipe.

This was a fun and easy casserole to make. Surprisingly low calorie for so much cheese. My husband, who doesn't like casseroles, really enjoyed this one. The grocery store didn't have summer squash, so I used the regular squash and cut down the amount. It worked wonderfully. I can really see adding more veggies to this casserole, as it has a lot of flexibility and flavor.

I love the foundation of this recipe –adding yellow squash to eggs. I did modify it , however. I grate the squash instead of slice it. I also add three times as many eggs and more milk. It turned out delicious and I make it all the time.
I made a slightly smaller version of this with one large summer squash. I liked it but think I would put a bit less butter in next time
I love it! I do not use any sugar or flour. It's wonderful without them!
I forgot the flour and it was still delicious! Make this casserole and make your people happy.

This is with out a doubt the best squash casserole I have ever had. I used seasoned salt and used pepper jack cheese along with the cheddar cheese and it turned out fabulous. I would recommend this to all. It is the consistency of a quiche.
